$comment: Shared session-clock fixture (parity audit row-03), consumed by the iOS MorseKitCheck harness, android SessionClockTest and desktop SessionClockTest. Data, not code - see CLAUDE.md's separate-ports rule. Expected values are derived from the rules in `derivation` (the iOS timer menu's documented behaviour, issue #41, and the run-out rule under `timeUp`), not captured from any implementation.

derivation.remaining: seconds left on the session countdown, or null for an open-ended session; 0 means the clock has run out and the session ends, or is held (see timeUp)
derivation.add: the timer menu's 'Add 5 minutes' / 'Add 1 minute': on a timed session the seconds are added to what is left; on an open-ended one they start a countdown of exactly that many seconds; a seconds value of zero or less changes nothing
derivation.subtract: the timer menu's 'Subtract 1 minute', offered only while the session is timed: what is left drops by the seconds, never below 0, and reaching 0 ends the session; an open-ended session has nothing to subtract from and stays open-ended; a seconds value of zero or less changes nothing
derivation.remove: 'Remove time limit' makes any session open-ended (remaining becomes null)
derivation.timeUp: when the countdown runs out while a drill has been sent and is waiting for its answer, the session is held: that drill can still be answered, and answering it ends the session where the next drill would have started. A hold lasts at most graceSeconds, so an abandoned session still ends. With nothing waiting it ends at once. `held` is whether the run-out found a drill waiting; `overdue` is the whole seconds since the countdown ran out; `expected` is whether the session ends now
derivation.firstSoundBeat: a session's first sound waits for its screen to arrive (an event, platform by platform), then `firstSoundBeat.seconds` more, so it does not land the instant the screen settles
derivation.note: Derived from these rules directly, independently of any implementation.
